correctness.rationale: Independently assembled the consistent mass and stiffness blocks and formed H=−(A+Aᵀ)/2 using MHM=(KM+MK)/2. Both matrices M and K are positive definite by their element quadratic forms and the zero boundary data; physical dissipation follows from d(cᵀMc)/dt=−2cᵀKc. H has positive diagonals and determinant equal to the stated positive factor times Δ, so Δ=0 is included in contractivity. Differentiating the squared Euclidean norm gives necessity and sufficiency over all times. When det H<0, −H has one positive eigenvalue and a positive off-diagonal, so a maximizing unit eigenvector has strictly positive coordinates. The symbolic replay gave Δ(1,r)=−P(r) and the four exact endpoint signs (+,−,−,+). Descartes' two sign changes and the two distinct brackets prove that both positive roots are simple and exhaust the positive roots; P(1)<0 determines the interior sign. The limiting scaled H and the mass eigenvalues reproduce the claimed coefficient and conditioning bound. The radical-to-trace ratio decreases for 0<r≤1, giving the stated supremum via r→0, not an attained maximum. The bound by √κ₂(M) distinguishes divergence of the initial rate from any divergence of finite-time amplification. With one degree of freedom A is a negative scalar. The two exact positive witnesses were also verified.
residual_risks: Only the 1-D three-element, two-interior-node consistent-P1 coefficient norm is classified. The algebraic and analytical argument, not mesh sampling, supplies the universal result.

value.rationale: A concrete smallest-dimension example is useful because stability in the physical energy and good mass conditioning do not certify monotonic nodal Euclidean decay. The full two-parameter criterion and the simple grading family with failure at both ends give exact benchmarks, and the thin-element calculation distinguishes arbitrarily steep initial growth from bounded amplification. These features are not supplied by just quoting dissipativity or exhibiting an arbitrary stable matrix.
residual_risks: Not a failure of physical stability, a time-integration claim, or a result about general meshes.
